claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys are single-phase hexagonal materials.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloys contain intrinsic residual stresses, dislocation networks, and nanoscale inhomogeneities produced by deposition.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with significant hysteresis.
Residual microstructural strains and dislocation networks govern the sharpness and hysteresis of the magnetocaloric response.
Residual strains and dislocation densities at grain boundaries and interfaces mediate coupling between magnetic and structural degrees of freedom.
High internal stress enforces rigid magnetostructural coupling and thereby creates a narrow, abrupt transition.
A mild post-deposition anneal at up to 500°C for 1–2 hours under inert atmosphere can relieve internal strain without causing phase separation or secondary-phase formation.
Relaxing residual strain makes the magnetostructural transformation less abrupt and permits more gradual magnetic-domain reorientation during thermal cycling.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, mild annealing will broaden the temperature interval over which magnetic entropy changes.
Relative to the as-deposited baseline, mild annealing will reduce maximum hysteresis losses.
Annealing may produce a smoother magnetization-versus-temperature curve.
Annealing may slightly lower the magnetic entropy change per unit applied field while improving reversibility.
Significant hysteresis in the as-deposited films limits heat-exchange capability and cooling-cycle efficiency.
The predicted effects apply near room temperature at an applied magnetic field of approximately 1 T.
The predicted effects are limited to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys made by the same deposition process and annealed below the threshold for phase changes.
Minor chemical inhomogeneities may also influence the magnetocaloric response.
High-entropy alloys have potential as magnetic refrigerants and may offer commercial and mechanical advantages over rare-earth-based refrigerants.

contradictions.description: The prediction is explicitly restricted to annealing that does not induce phase changes, but the falsification rule treats anneal-induced phase changes and deterioration as falsification. Such a result falls outside the stated boundary and would confound the strain-relief test rather than decisively falsify the proposed mechanism.
